key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term perovskite photoluminescence degradation from early time-series data, even for unseen material samples.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more informative stability screening of metal halide perovskites, reducing experimental testing time for solar-cell materials development.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 perovskite samples under heat and light stress.
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to encode degradation-relevant signal structure.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples and compared against baseline models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a diverse dataset of 167 materials and >86,000 PL spectra, with the proposed method generalizing across material groups and outperforming baseline benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the physics-informed features and the similarity of future materials to the training distribution.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
